question: Can the owner-locked presenter look be generated as native 9:16 portrait, and what does the full set cost?

draft_test.purpose: Prove the locked look survives recomposition from its landscape reference into portrait before committing a large spend.
draft_test.preset_declined: 24bae836-2c4a-48e0-89b6-49fcc0b21612 IN THE DARK, declined because a preset look would override the owner-locked look
observed: native 9:16 portrait, no crop from landscape
light blue chambray button-down, sleeves rolled to the forearm
seated at the wooden table in the inn breakfast room, window light from the left
likeness consistent with the locked still
recomposed so head and shoulders sit in the upper half, table edge below
hands resting on the table, camera locked off
natural interior, no studio lighting, no on-screen text
draft_test.limitation: A 6 second 480p draft establishes that the look and framing survive. It does not establish lip-sync drift over a long take, nor voice match, nor that any take is acceptable.

hard_constraint.finding: The full presenter set cannot be generated at 1080p on the current balance.
hard_constraint.note: Rates are measured by preflight on a 6 second 9:16 omni_reference call, not assumed. The earlier 9 credits per second figure came from the landscape long-form work and does not apply to portrait.

short_04_split.reason: Short 04's presenter close is 17.0s, inside the 16 to 24 second band that produced up to 1.5s of lip-sync drift on this episode's long form. Splitting it keeps every take inside the band that worked.
short_04_split.grammar_check: The owner-ruled grammar requires the presenter to return and land the conclusion. It does not require one take, and an internal cut inside the presenter movement is not a fourth movement.
short_04_split.status: agent decision, stated for the record

still_unruled: The beat assignment that defines all eight spans remains an agent reading, recorded in ep009-shorts-picture-grammar-v1. The owner ruled the three-movement grammar, not which paragraph sits in which movement.
not_authorized: the full presenter set at any resolution
lip sync, about 10.55 USD via Sync v3 for 1.32 minutes

closeup_test.purpose: Test the tighter phone-style opening the owner asked about, against the first seated medium-shot draft.
closeup_test.result: pass on framing and likeness, with one real loss
gained: face fills the frame and carries at phone size, which is what the opening needed
likeness and the chambray hold at close range
the inn window light and room read softly behind, so the locked setting survives
direct address is much stronger than the seated medium shot
lost: the hands are out of frame. The locked look has sleeves rolled to the forearm and the EP009 behaviour references carry contextual hand activity, and none of that is visible in a close-up this tight
the wooden table and the breakfast-room context are no longer legible, so the setting reads as a generic warm interior rather than the inn
closeup_test.reading: The close-up is right for the first beat and wrong as the whole opening. It solves the scroll-stop and loses the two things the look lock actually specifies. The fix is not to choose between them: open on this close-up, then settle back to the seated medium shot inside the same presenter movement. That is one state change, which U-05 allows, it breaks the eleven second static hold on Short 01, and it ends on the framing the look was locked at.
closeup_test.limitation: 480p draft, no audio, six seconds. Nothing here speaks to lip sync, voice match or an acceptable take.

opening_hold_finding.finding: Presenter share is not the outlier: our mean 0.441 against EP007's accepted 0.384. The opening hold is. Shorts 01 and 02 sit 4.4 and 3.3 seconds longer than EP007's accepted seven second open before any picture change. Cleo's 0.08 is not the right yardstick, because her visuals are spectacle that carries itself while ours are a procedure and a ledger.
opening_hold_finding.proposed_fix: Open tight, settle to medium inside the presenter movement. No word moves and the grammar is untouched.
opening_hold_finding.alternative_not_taken: Cutting the ratio itself would move words out of the presenter movements into the screens, which rewrites the beat assignment that is still unruled.
